erosion-filter.look: Relief: smooth 3-octave perlin hills whose flanks are carved by parallel V gullies running downhill, finer gullies feeding into coarser ones; hillshade top-down shows dendritic dark lines radiating from peaks and converging into valleys, flats stay smooth because of the slope mask. By far the most terrain-like result in the family. Defaults matter: one stripe per cell (sf=1) gives short starburst segments, sf=0.35 saturates to featureless ridges, sf=0.6 gives long coherent gullies; branch=1 makes fine stripes cross coarse ones (spiky herringbone), branch=0.3 gives tributaries. 3x3 polynomial-weight phacelle cells and the 4x4 exp window look identical in relief. Finite-difference gradient (eps 0.01) on the 3-octave base looks identical to the analytic gradient. A 5-octave fractal base scrambles the stripes into spikes, so the base must be smooth (3 octaves) or the gully scale must sit well below the base's finest octave.
erosion-filter.dims: 2D measured. 3D is heightfield form only: stripe lattice in the xz plane, y enters through the source; z-continuity max 0.014 per 1e-3 measured, XZ slice shows coherent gullies. No volumetric form. 4D not attempted.
erosion-filter.range: -0.77..0.88 over 8 seeds (base +-1 plus stripes 0.15*M); mean 0.07; far coords 4e4 fine, no NaN
erosion-filter.artifacts: Cell-boundary phase defects of the phacelle kernel are visible in the raw stripe field but hidden in the height output. c0ratio 6.3 with maxSlope 25: sign(S) tilt feedback and direction flips where the gradient passes through zero give steep but masked spots. Noisy (fractal) base gradients break the look. Mask uses an absolute slope reference, so it depends on the source gradient scale.
erosion-filter.node_shape: ErosionFilter modifier with Output enum; phacelle-noise lives inside as the Stripes output
erosion-filter.port_notes: Source evaluated dim+1 times once (forward differences measured fine); then a fixed Octaves loop of 3x3 cells with hash, polynomial weight, bounded-phase sincos, one sqrt, one pow for the detail mask (replace with a lerp). Members: Source, Octaves, Gully Scale, Strength, Lacunarity, Gain, Stripe Frequency (0.6), Branching, Detail, Slope Reference, Straight bool, Output enum {Height, Delta, Mask, Stripes}. 3D: pick the up axis, lattice in the other two.

critic.notes: The only method that makes branching drainage, on every seed and window tried (1337, 7, 99, 42, 2024 at windows 3 to 8). Amplitude is not the reason: rms(delta) was ridged .066, uber .021, swiss .030, slope aligned .061, erosion 2 oct .119, and with all of them scaled to match the rivals become spikes or lumps while the erosion filter still shows coherent gullies. Four real node graphs (12.5 to 16.3 ns) give no gullies: ridged plus altitude is good rugged terrain at half the price, warped ridged shows ribs only where the warp stretches, not downhill, warped cells are facets. Hessian via perlin2h does not pay: a plan curvature mask gives wormy hairlines (c0 2.51, max slope 72), a direction stability mask is amplitude invariant but softer with fewer gullies, curved phase only helps big cells (c0 6.41 -> 7.19 at s0 .3); a generic Source would need 6 evaluations for any of them. Weaknesses that remain: at wide views the gullies are short dashes of one size with a faint 6 armed star feel, and gully scale must be set against hill scale. Delta has mean +.10, so the node lifts terrain. 3D is heightfield only: raw vol shows vertical extrusions, h minus y density gives a proper surface. The altitude fade has the known weakness that a high valley stays gullied and a low peak goes smooth; altitude limits should be hybrids. Mask output is speckle, drop it from the Output enum.
critic.improved: Added an altitude fade to the flank mask plus a fade target (alt, altlo, althi, target in t_erosion_filter.cpp; t_erosion_filter.prev2.cpp is the version before this change). Valley floors now stay smooth while flanks keep their gullies, which the slope mask alone never did: on seed 7 at 3 octaves, max D8 flow accumulation 1848 -> 13775 and pits/1000px 4.74 -> 3.39. Cost is nil: 25.63 ns with it against 25.89 ns without at 2 octaves. Also cut stripe octaves from 3 to 2: 34.12 -> 25.89 ns in the AVX2 harness, and from the prototyper's 5 it is 50.28 -> 25.89 ns. With the fade on, 3 octaves are only slightly crisper than 2 at this view. Gallery sheet, thumb, relief, delta and finite difference overwritten; the first critic's versions are in critic1/, the prototyper's in prototyper/. Tried and rejected: V shaped channel floors (barely visible, c0 7.4 -> 4.5), 30 degree lattice rotation per octave (|c6| rises from .039-.045 to .058-.074), three Hessian uses (below).

Triangular halves the visible imprint and turns it 6 fold; it does not remove it. The first critic's axis4 metric could not see 6 fold.

A plain hypercubic 4D lattice (2^4 or 3^4 cells) gives a + weave and weak gullies, flat and on the torus.

critic.estimates: Estimates, not measured: 3D heightfield about 37 ns (3 x real FBm3 3D 6.80 + 16 ns stripes). 4D tile about 56 ns (3 x real FBm3 4D 12.47 + 16 ns stripes + 2 atan2). The harness uses a bounded phase polynomial sincos; FS::Sin and FS::Cos were not priced.

tournament.notes: The only method that makes branching drainage, on seeds 1337, 7, 99, 42, 2024 at windows 3 to 8, and this holds with amplitudes matched. Four real node graphs (12.5-16.3 ns) give no gullies. c0 6.2 to 7.1, no jumps; forward-difference far coords viewed fine at 4e4. Same-seed analytic and eps .01 forward-difference reliefs look identical. Remaining flaws: faint 6 fold imprint (|c6| .13-.15 at first octave), short same-size dashes at wide views, mean delta +.10, high valleys stay gullied and low peaks go smooth, so altitude limits should be hybrids. 3D is heightfield only; raw vol is vertical extrusions. Mask output is speckle, drop it. AVX2 numbers come from an intrinsics harness, not FastSIMD. FS::Sin/Cos were not priced, and 3D ~37 ns and 4D ~56 ns are estimates. Tile form is scalar proof only.

artist-terrain.note: Relief at seeds 1337 and 99 is the only true branching drainage in the set; smooth flats, fine gullies feeding coarse. ~20-25 ns AVX2 at 2 octaves (critic harness). c0 6.3. Faint 6-fold imprint. The terrain node.

master.one_liner: Modifier that adds branching drainage gullies to any height source, pointwise: stripes aligned to the slope in octaves, each octave steered by the previous one.
master.look: Prototype cl_misc node 5: plain fbm becomes eroded mountains with dendritic gullies running off ridges into smooth valleys, by far the most convincing terrain from any prototype here. Good for mountain heightfields, detail maps, ridge maps.
master.algorithm: Inputs: Source (height), Octaves, Gully Scale s0 (cells), Strength, Lacunarity, Gain, Branching, Detail, Slope Reference, Epsilon, Differences enum {Forward (d+1 evals), Central (2d+1)}. Step 1: h = Source(p); g = finite-difference gradient (2D: 2 or 4 extra evals). mask m = ease_out(|g|/SlopeRef) with ease_out(t) = 1-(1-sat(t))^2 (Runevision replaces sqrt to avoid discontinuity). G = g (working gradient), M = m (combined mask). Step 2, per octave o (fixed count): s = s0/lac^o, a = Strength*gain^o. Stripe normal n = perp(G)/max(|G|,eps) in 2D (gullies run along G, cross-section varies along n); 3D: n = normalize(G x Up) with Select fallback when parallel. Phacelle-style cell loop over 3x3 (or 4x4) cells of size s: pivot q_c = (c + rnd01^d(hash(seed,o,c)))*s; w_c = max(0, 1-|p-q_c|^2/(cut*s)^2)^2; phi_c = 2*pi*((p-q_c).n)/s; C += w_c cos(phi_c); S += w_c sin(phi_c). Normalise: L = sqrt(C^2+S^2); f = min(2L,1)/max(L,eps); C*=f; S*=f (only magnitudes > 0.5 are normalised, avoids spikes where waves cancel). Height delta: dh = a*M*C. Gully slope: slopeVec = -a*(2*pi/s)*sign(S)*n (sign gives straight triangle-wave gullies). Feedback: G += Branching*slopeVec (finer gullies tilt into coarser ones -> tributaries); newMask = sat(|S|) (zero at creases/ridges); M = (1-(1-M)^Detail)*newMask; h += dh. Output enum {Height = h, Delta = h - Source, Mask = M, RidgeMap (last octave faded toward 0)}.
master.why_new: Needs the source gradient and an orientation-driven noise, neither of which the graph can express (no derivative node, no anisotropic noise). Makes a hard thing (erosion without simulation) a one-node drop-in on any height graph, and it stays pointwise so it works with GenPositionArray and chunked generation.
master.simd_plan: Source evals dim+1 once. Inner cost octaves*window^d iterations of hash + weight + sin + cos; octave count is constant so the loop is legal. Estimated 30-40 ns/sample AVX2 in 2D at 4 octaves (about 30x Perlin; scalar sketch measured 31x Perlin with a 3-octave FBm base). Reductions: 3x3 window with R up to 1.25 and small jitter, polynomial cos. 3D: run the 2D lattice on a chosen plane and pass the third axis to Source, same cost. 4D tiling: 2^4 cells, R about 1, near-zero jitter (t = J*g with pairs xy, zw). Cost is justified only by the result, so it is a finishing node, not a building block.
master.continuity: Delta field is C1 away from stripe cancellation points (handled by the k=2 clamp) and from |G|->0 (masked to zero by M). Simple per-lane direction gives visible direction discontinuities where G turns fast (Runevision accepts this because the mask hides them). Overall continuity = min(source, C0).
master.params: Source (GeneratorSource), Octaves (int, ~5), Lacunarity (2), Gain (0.5), Strength (hybrid), SlopeStrength (~3), BranchStrength (~3), Cell Scale (erosion feature size), Stripe Frequency, Step (gradient epsilon, hybrid), WaterLevel / ValleyAlt / PeakAlt (hybrid), Detail, GullyWeight, StraightGullies (bool), Output enum.
master.risks:
LICENSE: the gist says its erosion function derives from Gavoronoise under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, while FastNoise2 is MIT; reimplement from the mathematical description in Johansen's blog and check provenance before shipping. Cost. A fractal base's gradient is noisy at fine scale and scrambles stripes, so low octave bases work best. True 4D or tileable form is unproven.
[ErosionFilter, libs-modifiers] High cost. Distortion when the gradient changes sharply within a cell. Altitude-based fade target fails where a valley sits above a peak. Gullies do not form true connected drainage. It is a heightfield idea, so 3D is plane-based. My prototype is a sketch rather than the author's code, so the real look depends on a port; check the licence of his code before porting (one port is reported as MPL-2.0 with his permission).
[ErosionFilter, nature-phenomena] The Bevy port warns against finite-differenced gradients, since they break consistency between height and gradient, and FastNoise has no analytic gradients. This is the main technical risk. My crude reimplementation with FD did not reproduce branching gullies with either stripe form, but it omitted some masks and tuning, so it says nothing about the real filter. Substituting 4-corner stripes looked the same as 16-kernel stripes in that crude test, which needs retesting once the base look works. Shader code is on Shadertoy under MPL-2.0 per the search summary, so confirm the licence before porting.
[ErosionFilter, repo-demand] Shader code is MPL-2.0, so derive from the article or ask. Needs source range knowledge for the fade target (connects to #121). Gradient by stencil multiplies source cost. The article does not cover 3D, so the 3D form here is my extension. Altitude-based fade misbehaves where valleys are higher than distant peaks (author notes this).
master.cost_note: Estimated 30-40 ns/sample AVX2 in 2D at 4 octaves (about 30x Perlin; scalar sketch measured 31x Perlin with a 3-octave FBm base).
master.variant_notes: Seven independent proposals of the Fewes/clayjohn/Johansen technique. One crude reimplementation (nature-phenomena) did not reproduce branching gullies, and the Bevy port warns against finite-differenced gradients: treat the look as unconfirmed until a port matches the author's. Licences differ by source (CC BY-NC-SA, MPL-2.0, MIT): implement from the description only.

fractal-derivative.look: Not a gully method: none of the four modes produces gullies or drainage lines. What it does give, and plain ridged/FBm cannot: Uber (ridge + altitude erosion + slope erosion) turns the busy ridged field into smooth sediment-filled bowls and flats with all the fine detail concentrated on the crests and rims, like eroded highlands with filled valleys. Swiss gives knife crests and smooth valleys with some downhill streaking on the flanks from the dsum warp. Jordan gives soft billowy domes rising from flats. iq is just softened FBm. Warp 0.2-0.5 adds mild sweeping to the bowls. Visibly different from the plain ridged baseline in the same relief, mainly through the smooth valleys.
fractal-derivative.dims: 2D and 3D measured (perlin3g/simplex3g gradients; vol render shows solid 3D lobes); 4D not prototyped, loop is dimension agnostic

fractal-derivative.artifacts: Output range is data dependent (erosion only subtracts, so sum/norm is biased: uber mean 0.39, jordan heavily skewed). Altitude erosion with sat(height) flattens everything below mid height, so bowls read as lakes at the relief clip. The n*dn ridge derivative substitute works (no jump measured at sharp=-1).

fractal-derivative.port_notes: Needs a value+gradient kernel per basis. Fixed-count loop, feedback is FMAs plus one reciprocal per octave; per-octave rotation is a fixed matrix on p and the accumulators. Uber knobs cover iq and most of Swiss; Jordan needs its own n^2 accumulators. Ship Uber + Swiss + Jordan as a Mode enum with Sharpness, Slope Erosion, Altitude Erosion, Perturb hybrids, and a measured VariableRange table per mode.

critic.notes: Not the gully winner but the cheap tier. The prototyper's 'no mode produces gullies' is too strong for Swiss on its own base: at warp .15 to .3 steep flanks carry long parallel flutes running downhill, and in relief those read as gullies at 45 percent of the erosion filter's price. They do not branch and they only exist on steep ridged walls. The shared base test hides this because Swiss detail on a smooth base has rms .030 and no walls to flute. 'A look ridged and graphs cannot make' is false for Uber: real FractalRidged Weighted=1 gives the same crests and bowls at 6.58 ns against 9.19 ns. Jordan at seed 42 is domes on a rough sea with mean -.70, not worth a mode. 3D: uber and swiss at iso 0 are almost solid with a few holes because of the positive mean, so the prototyper's 'solid 3D lobes' overstates it; this is a terrain fractal. It cannot take a Source without forward differences per octave, so it needs its own value + gradient Perlin kernel; that kernel costs 4.44 vs 3.47 ns over 3 octaves.
critic.improved: No code change. Warp sweep on seed 99: .08 c0 4.77, .15 c0 4.04, .3 c0 2.63 with max slope 60. Flutes get bolder with warp, .15 is the last value I trust.

tournament.notes: Ship narrowed to Swiss on Perlin basis, as the cheap fluted alpine tier: 11.52 ns, 1.77x ridged, 45 percent of the erosion filter. Long parallel flutes down steep walls read as gullies in relief but do not branch, and they need ridged walls, so a smooth shared base hides them. Uber is a preset of real FractalRidged Weighted=1 (6.58 vs 9.19 ns). Jordan at seed 42 is domes on a rough sea with mean -.70, not worth a mode. Swiss on Simplex breaks: c0 1.81, max slope 297. Swiss c0 3.6-4.0 is steep folds, not jumps; range mean +.27, so it needs a measured scale. A terrain fractal, not a volume: vol at iso 0 is almost solid. Needs its own value+gradient Perlin kernel, because a Source would cost forward differences per octave.

master.one_liner: Fractal with an internal derivative-capable basis and per-octave derivative feedback: No Man's Sky Uber noise (sharpness, slope erosion, altitude erosion, perturb), de Carpentier's Swiss and Jordan turbulence, and IQ's derivative fbm in one node.
master.look:
Prototype cl_flowfrac: Damp .15 on ridged gives clean thin connected ridge networks; on FBm gives smooth slopes with detail only on flats, like eroded or wind-scoured land. Swirl at .03-.1 pulls fine octaves along coarse contours: flowing streaks and crumpled silk; Swirl .25+ gives topographic hair lines. Advect darkens creases like wrinkled skin.
[FractalUber, terrain-tools-engines] Eroded-looking mountains with sharp ridges and smooth sediment-filled valleys (slope erosion flattens where accumulated gradient is high), billowy Jordan hills with gully-like warps, Swiss sharp crests. Visibly different from FBm/Ridged: valleys are flat, ridges are knife-like, detail is where slopes are.
master.algorithm: Internal basis enum {Simplex (OpenSimplex2 with analytic gradient), Perlin (quintic, gradient via de Carpentier's dn formulas), Value (IQ noised)} returning (n, dn). Common loop, fixed Octaves: sum=0, amp=1, freq=1, dsum=0(vec), dwarp=0(vec). Octave o: pos = p*freq + Warp*dwarp (Swiss: (p + warp*dsum)*freq); (n,dn) = basis(seed+o, pos); Sharpness s in [-1,1]: billow = 2|n|-1, ridge = 1-2|n|; n' = lerp(n, billow, max(s,0)); n' = lerp(n', ridge, max(-s,0)); dn' uses n*dn in place of sign(n)*dn (de Carpentier's artifact-free substitute). Altitude erosion: a_o = amp * lerp(1, clamp(sum,0,1), AltitudeErosion). Slope erosion: a_o *= 1/(1 + SlopeErosion*dot(dsum,dsum)) (IQ 1/(1+d.d)). sum += a_o*n'; dsum += a_o*dn'; dwarp += Perturb*n*dn (Jordan's warp accumulator); freq*=Lacunarity; amp*=Gain; optional per-octave rotation of p (2D 2x2 matrix [0.8,-0.6;0.6,0.8], 3D fixed rotation). Mode presets: Swiss = {ridge, dsum += amp*dn*(-n), amp *= gain*clamp(sum,0,1), pos=(p+warp*dsum)*freq, defaults gain 0.6 warp 0.15}; Jordan = {n2 = n*n, sum += damped*n2, dwarp += warp*n*dn, ddamp += damp*n*dn, damped = amp*(1 - dampScale/(1+dot(ddamp,ddamp))), defaults gain1 0.8 gain 0.5 warp0 0.4 warp 0.35 damp0 1 damp 0.8}; IQ = {raw n, a_o = amp/(1+dot(dsum,dsum))}. Output ScaleOutput by analytic amplitude bound (VariableRange).
master.why_new: Nodes output one float, so octave-to-octave gradient feedback cannot be built in a graph; finite-difference emulation would cost 3-5 evals per octave and still cannot warp by the accumulated gradient. This is the single most cited 'how do AAA terrain look good' trick (NMS GDC 2017, de Carpentier, Elevated).
master.simd_plan:
Constant octave loop, all formulas branch free. Fork's measurements, AVX2, Simplex, 5 octaves, 4096 points: FBm 38.5 / 76.7 / 105 us; analytic damped 56.2 / 107.4 / 214.8 us; forward differences 120 / 267.9 / 470.9 us (2D/3D/4D). So about 1.4 to 2x FBm with analytic gradients. Swiss and Jordan add only a position add per octave.
[FractalGradientFeedback, lit-classic] Fixed loop: Octaves x (d+1) Source evals with FD = 3x/4x/5x FractalFBm cost. 2D 6 octaves of Simplex ~20 ns; analytic gradient drops it to ~1.3x FBm (see notes on a Gradient virtual). Scalar 8.9x perlin2 at 6 octaves using analytic derivatives. Same GenT structure as FractalFBm, members are hybrids sampled once per Gen.
master.continuity: C0 in theory. Prototype c0ratio 7.5 at 2 octaves, falling to 2.85 at 6 octaves because domain feedback compounds slope (slope effect, not a jump). The ridged+damp case with sign-based gradient measured 1.18, a true jump, so the -n*g form is mandatory.
master.params: Basis enum, Octaves (int), Lacunarity, Gain (hybrid), Sharpness -1..1 (hybrid), Slope Erosion (hybrid), Altitude Erosion (hybrid), Perturb/Warp (hybrid), Damping (Jordan), Octave Rotation (bool), Mode enum {Uber, Swiss, Jordan, IQ}, Feature Scale, Seed Offset.
master.risks:
Many knobs; amplitude normalisation is data dependent (slope erosion reduces amplitude unpredictably) so Output Min/Max will be approximate; derivative accumulation in 4D doubles register pressure.
[FractalDerivative, repo-demand] GenGradient touches every coherent generator's kernel and dispatch. Overlaps upstream plans, so coordinate with existing fork design. Fork reported an unexplained 32-bit MSVC AVX512 build failure. Fractal range is unbounded (#212 complaints) and damping complicates normalising further.
[FractalGradientFeedback, lit-classic] Advect or Swirl above small values alias quickly, since feedback amplifies per octave; recommended range is narrow, perhaps scale by 1/f. Output needs clamp. FD on non-smooth Sources gives noisy directions. Swirl 3D form untested.
master.cost_note: So about 1.4 to 2x FBm with analytic gradients.
master.variant_notes: Unified loop covering IQ slope damping, Swiss, Jordan, Uber (sharpness, altitude erosion, perturb) and flow-noise advection. The Swiss -n*g form is mandatory: a sign(n)*g form measured a real jump. A fork has already merged the damped mode with analytic gradients, with AVX2 numbers in simd_plan.

queue.name: FractalDerivative
queue.reason: Uber, Swiss and iq derivative fBm: the most demanded terrain fractal, 1.4-2x FBm measured on a fork (J1, J2, J4 top pick). Its gradient basis is plumbing for ~15 other ideas, so build it first and diet the knobs.

fractal-slope-aligned.look: Gullies mode: hills whose flanks carry fine radial fibres running straight downhill, like fluted or badland slopes; top-down hillshade shows feathery streaks fanning out from every peak and converging in the valleys. It reads as downhill grain, not as branching gullies: the rills are thin, equal and un-nested. Strata mode: fine detail elongated along contours gives swirling flow-marble bands wrapping the hills, a striking look nothing on the existing sheet has. Both relax to isotropic FBm on flats. The catalogue's coordinate-stretch formulation (frame=0) is unusable: q' = M q multiplies an absolute position by a spatially varying matrix, giving scribbled swirls, c0ratio 1.2 and maxSlope 667.
fractal-slope-aligned.dims: 2D and 3D measured (elliptical simplex2/simplex3 kernels; vol render is solid 3D with streaky surfaces); 4D not prototyped, kernel generalises
fractal-slope-aligned.range: -0.85..0.88 over 8 seeds, mean 0; far coords fine; aniso=0 degenerates exactly to simplex FBm (c0 8.0)
fractal-slope-aligned.artifacts: Unsolved flaw: the frame may only come from the first octave (fo=1). Letting anisotropic octaves steer later frames compounds into near-jumps (c0ratio 6.9 at 2 octaves, 2.0 at 3, 1.8 at 5 with fo=2), because a compressed octave's gradient swings 4x faster along its narrow axis; so the spec's accumulated frame does not hold and detail does not nest. High aniso compresses the finest octave below pixel size (aliasing in 640 px renders at aniso 3 with 5-6 octaves). Elongation is capped near the kernel radius; at aniso 5 the lattice shows as sliver gaps.
fractal-slope-aligned.node_shape: Frame mode of FractalDerivative (Simplex basis), or standalone AnisoSimplex fractal with Mode {Gullies, Strata}, Aniso, Sensitivity, Drift, Damp, Frame Octaves
fractal-slope-aligned.port_notes: Elliptical kernel = normal simplex corner loop with the offset passed through a symmetric DxD matrix (3 FMAs 2D, 6 3D per corner) before falloff and gradient dot; continuity preserved because |M d| >= |d| keeps the kernel inside the r^2 = 0.5 support. Gradient needs the same matrix back. Fits inside FractalDerivative as Frame {None, Gullies, Strata} with Aniso and Sensitivity, frame from the first octave or a Direction source.

critic.notes: As a gully method it loses on price: 12.23 ns against 12.36 ns for one erosion octave, and the erosion octave shows real gullies while this shows needle grass at any amplitude. Rills are thin, equal and do not nest, because the frame may only come from the first octave. Strata is the part worth keeping: contour wrapping flow bands at window 3 are distinctive, soft and cheap. At window 6 on seeds 42 and 99 it thins to blobs with contour lines, so it is a close range material look. The 3D vol at iso 0 is messy sheets on solids, and Gullies in 3D is pockmarked rather than streaky as the prototyper wrote. I disagree with folding it into fractal-derivative: Swiss only works on Perlin (c0 1.81 on Simplex) and this only works on Simplex, so they share no basis and the merged node would need modes that forbid each other's basis. Niche and cheap, so include it as an example. If a steered anisotropic simplex node is ever built for other reasons, Strata becomes a recipe on it. Coordinate stretch form confirmed broken in the image: scribble, c0 1.2.
critic.improved: Nothing better found. Same altitude fade as the erosion filter applied to the Gullies frame: it fixes the valley floors but the flanks still read as needles. Strata images at other seeds and a wider window added.

tournament.notes: Gullies frame should not ship: 12.23 ns against 12.36 ns for one erosion octave, and it reads as needle grass at any amplitude. Frame comes from octave 0 only, so rills do not nest. Strata is the part to keep: soft contour-wrapping flow bands at window 3, cheap at 7.99 ns (1.20x FBm5 simplex). At window 6 on seeds 42 and 99 it thins to blobs with contour lines, and the vol is messy sheets on solids, so it is a close range material look. Disagrees with both the prototyper and the first critic on folding it into fractal-derivative: Swiss needs Perlin and this needs Simplex, so they share no basis. Niche, so an example rather than a mode. Coordinate stretch form confirmed broken in the image (c0 1.2).

graphics-researcher.note: Gullies mode is needle grass, but the Strata mode (detail elongated along contours, flow-marble wrapping every hill) is a genuinely new organisation of detail by landform at 1.2x FBm. Frame-from-first-octave limit is honest.

master.one_liner: FBm where each finer octave is sampled in an anisotropic frame built from the accumulated gradient of the coarser octaves, so detail becomes gullies running downhill or strata lines running along contours.
master.look: Terrain whose fine detail is organised by the big shapes: parallel rills/gullies that run down the flanks of coarse hills (Gullies), or layered ledges that wrap around hills like contour lines (Strata). On flats it relaxes to isotropic noise. Nothing on the contact sheet has orientation that follows the landform; FBm detail is isotropic everywhere. Good for DEM-like terrain, dunes (features perpendicular to a wind direction derived from the coarse field), lichen/bark growth along gradients, and as a heightmap whose hillshade reads as eroded.
master.algorithm:
Needs value+gradient per octave: use an internal gradient-returning Simplex/Perlin (iq 'noised' style; the existing gradient kernels already have the dot products, derivative adds ~50%). Pseudo (dimension agnostic, vectors are D-vectors):
  F=0; G=0 (D-vec); amp=1; freq=1
  for i in 0..Octaves-1 (uniform loop):
    g = G * Sensitivity                       // accumulated slope so far
    m2 = dot(g,g); n = g * InvSqrt(m2 + 1)    // |n|<1, ->0 on flats (regularised, no branch)
    s = 1 + Aniso * Sqrt(m2/(m2+1))           // stretch factor, 1 on flats
    // Gullies: elongate features along the slope direction -> M = I + (s-1)(|n|^2 I - n n^T)
    // Strata : elongate features along contours        -> M = I + (s-1) n n^T
    q = p*freq + Drift * G                    // optional downhill(+)/uphill(-) drift of the lattice (iq)
    q' = M * q                                 // 2D: 4 FMAs; 3D: 9
    (v, dv) = noised(q', seed+i)
    damp = 1 / (1 + Damp * dot(G,G))          // optional iq erosion damping
    F += amp*damp*v
    G += amp*damp*freq * (M^T dv)             // chain rule, frame derivative ignored (look only)
    amp*=Gain; freq*=Lacunarity
  out = F / sum(amp_i)
Enum Mode {Gullies, Strata}. Drift, Damp, Aniso, Sensitivity are the knobs; Aniso 0 and Drift 0 and Damp 0 degenerate to plain FBm.
master.why_new: A graph cannot access gradients of a node (scalar outputs only), so no graph can orient one octave by another. DomainWarp stretches detail but with no relation to slope; this is the first node where the frame of octave i+1 is a function of d/dp of octaves <= i.
master.simd_plan: Branch-free by construction (regularised normalisation, Select-free). Needs a GradSimplex/GradPerlin internal kernel for 2D, 3D, 4D (iq noised generalises; in 4D the M matrix is 16 FMAs). No lattice window beyond the kernel's own. Cost per octave ~1.6x Simplex (gradient) + 10-25 FMAs for the frame => 5 octaves roughly 12-14 ns/sample 2D on AVX2 vs 5.5 for FBm Simplex 5; about 2x an equivalent FBm. A generic-source variant using finite differences costs (D+1) source evals per octave; offer it only as 'any source' fallback.
master.continuity: C1 when the internal noise is C2 (Simplex/quintic Perlin): the frame depends on the gradient (C1) and composition keeps C1. Drift and Damp are smooth functions of G. No discontinuities anywhere.
master.params: Source kernel enum (GradSimplex/GradPerlin), Octaves int, Gain hybrid, Lacunarity float, Mode enum, Aniso hybrid (0..4, spatially variable is useful), Sensitivity float, Drift hybrid (signed), Damp hybrid, Seed Offset.
master.risks: Large Aniso with high Lacunarity can alias (features compressed below sample spacing); clamp s*freq. Ignoring the frame derivative in the gradient update is an approximation; it only affects how later octaves are oriented, not continuity. 4D version is expensive (mainly for tiling).
master.cost_note: Cost per octave ~1.6x Simplex (gradient) + 10-25 FMAs for the frame => 5 octaves roughly 12-14 ns/sample 2D on AVX2 vs 5.5 for FBm Simplex 5; about 2x an equivalent FBm.

phacelle-noise.look: Raw stripe field steered by the base gradient: zebra bands following the slope with soft cell-boundary dislocations and saturated ridges from the magnitude normalisation. As the erosion kernel, the 3x3 polynomial-weight window (cut 1.25, jitter in 0.25..0.75) is visually identical to the 4x4 exp window in relief, so the cheaper window is the one to port. Written clean from the maths, no reference code used.
phacelle-noise.dims: 2D lattice; used in the erosion filter's 3D heightfield form on the xz plane
phacelle-noise.artifacts: Direction undefined where the gradient vanishes (handled by the slope mask in the filter, visible as swirl defects in the raw output). Per-cell phase offsets make stripes incoherent across cells at one stripe per cell; 0.6 stripes per cell is the coherent regime.
phacelle-noise.node_shape: Stripes output of ErosionFilter; a standalone node would be the same 3x3 loop with an Angle hybrid or Direction source
phacelle-noise.port_notes: Same 3x3 window and bounded-phase sincos as the filter; constant-direction use collapses to one sincos.

As a standalone node it does not earn its 8 ns: gradient driven raw output has hairline arcs at direction singularities, and the clean angle driven form covers the zebra niche already held by the stripes family (lattice-phasor, vortex-phase). The first critic's 'defect ridden' applies to the gradient driven form only. 3x3 polynomial and 4x4 exp kernels do look alike in relief, but both square forms carry the + weave; port the triangular 3x3.
critic.improved: Tested the catalogue's other input, an angle field from slow noise instead of a gradient (t_gully_h.cpp). With no critical points the singular hairlines go away: c0 7.8 to 8.0 against 1.40 triangular and 1.51 square for gradient driven raw output at seed 99 (max slope above 1300). It reads as zebra or labyrinth stripes. Still biased, mean +.54, and rows from the lattice show when the field is nearly straight.

plan_node.expected_cost: Measured with fnlab bench, min of 3 runs, 2 stripe octaves on a 3 octave Perlin FBm, clang-cl 23. AVX2 29.56 / 42.60 / 69.92 ns, SSE41 66.74 / 91.15 / 155.40, AVX512 19.23 / 26.63 / 54.35. That FBm alone is AVX2 3.12 / 6.58 / 12.24, so 4 taps are 12.5 / 26.3 / 49.0. On plain Perlin AVX2 19.62 / 24.66 / 36.81. Stripe octaves on the FBm, AVX2 2D: 1 is 20.86, 3 is 36.05, about 8 ns each. Hand harness estimates were 25.6 / 37 / 56 with forward differences.
plan_node.dims: 2D, 3D and 4D measured. 3D is a heightfield: lattice in the two axes other than Up Axis, the up axis only reaches the source. 4D serves GenTileable2D only: lattice on the angles of (x, z) and (y, w) with whole cell counts from the radii. The tile closes, but other 4D positions jump where a count changes (fnlab seams 4D: 3655 of 4000, worst 0.306), and the description says so.
plan_node.range: Output stays in source units, so no ScaleOutput and no VariableRange. Delta is bounded by Strength * (1 - Gain^octaves) / (1 - Gain). Measured on a normalised FBm3 over 8 seeds: Height -0.781..0.871, Delta -0.150..0.192, mean +0.046. Mask is exactly -1..1.
notes: Remaining weaknesses: short dashes of one size at wide views, faint 6-fold imprint (|c6| .13 to .15), heightfield only.
Reimplement from the maths: the reference gist derives from CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 code. The Phacelle reference is MPL-2.0, so write that clean too.

master.one_liner: Cell-blended stripes that follow an input direction field with constant width: leaf veins and drainage patterns, and the base of the runevision erosion filter.
master.look: With a field from low-frequency noise: leaf venation, river deltas, feather barbs, radiating streaks with forks. Constant direction: zebra lines with soft defects. Prototype: dcc_lens mode=15.
master.algorithm: Input direction dir at p: Angle (hybrid), or gradient of a Field source by forward difference, normalised. side = perp(dir)*Frequency*TAU. For each cell in the 3^dim window: h=hash(cell); c=cell+0.25+0.5*rnd(h) per axis; v=p-c; wgt=Max(0,1-dot(v,v)/1.5625)^3; ph=dot(v,side); C+=wgt*Cos(ph); S+=wgt*Sin(ph); W+=wgt. Then C/=W; S/=W; m=Max(1-Norm, Sqrt(C*C+S*S)); out=S/m. Original uses 4x4 with exp(-2 r2) minus a constant; my look test shows tight-jitter 3x3 with this polynomial is visually equal.
master.why_new: Stripes aligned to an arbitrary field at constant width and without looping artifacts; warping a sine does neither. Cost is a fraction of Phasor per the author's count (16 loops vs 144-400). Erosion filter ports already exist for Blender and Houdini, so demand is real.
master.simd_plan: 9/27/81 sites with Sin+Cos each, about 13 / 40 / 120 ns (12x/18x/28x Perlin) plus (dim+1) Field evals. 4x4 window is 16/64/256 and not worth it. Constant direction collapses to one sincos, which is CarrierStripes territory. Bounded phase allows polynomial sincos.
master.continuity: Constant direction with Norm<1: C0, measured c0ratio 8.0 at Norm 0.25-0.75; Norm=1 gives jumps (1.81). Direction from a gradient field: jumps at the field's critical points (measured 1.53), because a unit direction is undefined there. Fix by fading stripe amplitude toward 0 as |grad| goes to 0, as the erosion post does.
master.params: Frequency (hybrid), Angle (hybrid) or Field (GeneratorSource), Offset (hybrid, shifts phase), Norm (hybrid), Grid Jitter (float, capped).
master.risks:
Singular points in the direction field need the fade. MPL-2.0 applies to the author's code; a clean implementation from this description should be checked against that. 3D direction needs a chosen perpendicular, since a side vector is underdetermined; author's post covers 2D only.
[PhacelleStripes, repo-demand] Too few cells per stripe gives grain, too many turns all ridge (author). Reimplement from the blog since shader code is MPL-2.0. Output depends on Direction being normalised. No prototype run by me.
master.cost_note: 9/27/81 sites with Sin+Cos each, about 13 / 40 / 120 ns (12x/18x/28x Perlin) plus (dim+1) Field evals.
master.variant_notes: Kept apart from PhasorNoise because one direction is shared by all kernels per lane, which is the source of its cost saving. PhasorCellNoise is credited here for its Spread=0 'in unison' mode.
